query: How do proportional-sharing, capped-per-node, and winner-takes-all collision models compare analytically for regret, feasibility, and long-run allocation fairness?

response.query: How do proportional-sharing, capped-per-node, and winner-takes-all collision models compare analytically for regret, feasibility, and long-run allocation fairness?
response.answer: Proportional-sharing minimizes regret, capped-per-node ensures feasibility, and winner-takes-all maximizes fairness for the most dominant users. Long-run allocation fairness varies significantly among these models.

results.title: The Unfinished Story - A Translated Story - PriyaBharati
results.content: He says he’s all about the middle class but his plans hurt the middle class all the way down. How much do we have to take before we all say enough?
